tldr: Eccentric Molecules and Flare orders now flow end to end; Shopify parity items (one connector per store, line-level attributes) are live in production.
Snap performance is degrading ahead of peak after their version upgrades; Ryan is working with Synergy Direct, and the risk is delayed orders reaching the WMS, not lost orders.
Raw transaction history will likely spill into next sprint because work order and pick/pack feedback was reprioritised ahead of CT, and about half the team is off ill.
Stock by location is grouped into the Shopify Jitterbit parity work, which probably won't start at the beginning of November.
Sister Co orders into Snap still fail with invalid API credentials; a special-character issue in generated passwords is suspected and a new host is being set up.
decisions: Stock by location is folded into the Shopify Jitterbit parity initiative.
Work order and pick/pack feedback is fixed before the CT work, to avoid duplicate feedback, and this delays the raw transaction history.
Compare the broken-down Shopify requirements list against the reviewed client extracts when the Jitterbit parity work starts.

actions.text: Update the group on the Snap performance issue once Ryan reports back from Synergy Direct.
Close out stock sync and stock API QA.
Make, test and get sign-off on the minor work order and pick/pack rework.
Hold the Friday session to start plotting customer migration dates.
Share a more detailed January to March roadmap of customer dates at next week's meeting.
Regenerate the Sister Co Snap API password without special characters and retest after the call.
Rename the new Snap host to match the current Fuse naming convention and confirm Snap have promoted the changes for it.
Create the new host and retry getting Sister Co orders from Fuse into Snap.

questions: Will the Snap degradation delay orders into the WMS at peak volumes, and can Synergy Direct find the cause?
Is the Snap invalid API credentials error caused by special characters in passwords, or by something else?
Is the Snap credentials issue likely to hit other customers?
Which Shopify Jitterbit parity items are needed first, and which customers can move in January versus March?
Does the production date field in returns goods mapping matter for any client-specific need?
